children: Round-up of South Korean financial markets:
** South Korean shares cut early gains to close marginally higher on Tuesday on caution over oil prices ahead of a holiday period.
** The benchmark KOSPI
closed up 10.19 points, or 0.15%, at 7,017.91, after rising as much as 2.3% earlier in the session.
** In afternoon trading, the index briefly turned lower.
** "There is caution ahead of a local holiday period, and there still are concerns over oil prices and bond yields," said Huh Jae-hwan, an analyst at Eugene Investment Securities.
** Local financial markets will be closed on Thursday and Friday for Chuseok holidays.

** Oil prices gained for the first time in five sessions as investors awaited developments on potential US-Iran talks at the United Nations General Assembly this week after more supplies emerged through the Strait of Hormuz over the weekend.

** A board member of the Bank of Korea said the central bank would determine the timing and pace of further interest rate hikes by closely assessing inflation, economic growth and financial stability.
** Chipmaker Samsung Electronics
rose 0.91%, while peer SK Hynix
lost 1.50%.
** Nuclear energy-related and construction stocks rose on hopes of a boost from South Korea's plans for US investments, with KEPCO Engineering & Construction
rising 6.6% and Taihan Cable & Solution
gaining 6.4%. Doosan Enerbility
rose 1.4%, while Hyundai Engineering & Construction
climbed 4.5%.

** South Korea confirmed its first project under a $350 billion US investment pact and said it is considering two others, moving ahead despite profitability concerns and criticism from President Donald Trump over the pace of implementation.
** Of the total 914 traded issues, 383 shares advanced, while 463 declined.
** Foreigners were net buyers of shares worth 76.2 billion won ($56.02 million).
** The won was quoted at 1,358.2 per dollar on the onshore settlement platform
, 1.27% higher than its previous close at 1,375.4.
** The most liquid three-year Korean treasury bond yield (KR3YT=RR) fell by 1.5 basis points to 4.040%, while the benchmark 10-year yield
rose by 1.4 basis points to 4.460%.
